dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: Overview of active protections
dashboard.weekBarSelectHint: Show app usage for this day in the chart
dashboard.noFixedCap: No fixed daily cap (see Screen Time).
dashboard.trackedAppOverlap: Tracked app minutes can exceed session minutes when several catalog apps run at the same time.

webFilter.title: Web Filter
webFilter.subtitle: Block websites and domains via /etc/hosts
webFilter.enableWebFilterHint: When enabled, configured domains are blocked via /etc/hosts.
webFilter.noDomainsYet: No custom domains yet. Add below or enable category lists (HaGeZi) in Quick Add.
webFilter.updateListsTitle: Download newer HaGeZi list versions when online (see README)
webFilter.clearAllConfirmMsg: Clear all custom domains and disable all category lists ({count} sources)? Click Apply afterwards to write to /etc/hosts.
webFilter.rulesApplied: Rules applied to /etc/hosts — DNS cache flushed
webFilter.allowed: Allowed: {host} (removed from block set if present)

appControl.title: App Control
appControl.subtitle: Block applications from launching via desktop file overrides
appControl.enableAppControlHint: When enabled, app blocking and daily app quotas are enforced.
appControl.applyTitle: Apply blocked apps and quota limits
appControl.dailyLimits: Daily time limits for individual apps
appControl.noQuotasForAccount: No quotas apply to this Linux account (or add a limit with this account below). "All accounts" limits always apply when that user is signed in.
appControl.processRequired: Process name is required for each row.
appControl.resetTodayMsg: Delete today's quota-usage file? All "used today" minutes reset to 0; counting resumes on the next enforcement tick.

schedules.title: Screen Time
schedules.subtitle: Set daily limits and allowed usage hours
schedules.presetsHint: School / Leisure templates (Screen Time only). Adjust and click Apply Changes.
schedules.presetConfirmMsg: Load the "{preset}" preset now? Unsaved changes on this page will be overwritten.
schedules.enableScreenTimeHint: When enabled, the LiFE Parental Control process enforces limits every minute.
schedules.todayAllowance: Today's allowance includes +{min} min added by a parent (logged usage is unchanged).
schedules.resetCounterHint: Start today's tally over (removes today's usage file). No password — use for mistakes or testing.
schedules.limitReachedHint: When the limit is reached, this app shows a dialog to add more time with the parent password (no separate bonus form here).
schedules.midnightHint: If From is later than To (e.g. 22:00–07:00), the allowed window spans midnight.
schedules.noHistoryYet: No history files in config dir yet.
schedules.presetApplied: Preset applied — click Apply Changes to apply on the system
schedules.resetTodayMsg: Reset today's screen time counter to 0? Removes today's usage file; counting continues on the next enforcement tick.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Password protection and application configuration
settings.nodeNotFound: /usr/bin/node not found — the daemon requires Node.js. Install the nodejs package, then install the daemon.
settings.appArmor_disabled: AppArmor is disabled in the kernel — blocking may not work.
settings.appArmor_parser_missing: Missing apparmor_parser — AppArmor profiles cannot be loaded.
settings.appArmor_profile_missing: Missing AppArmor profile /etc/apparmor.d/life-parental-blocked — blocking may not be enforced.
settings.appArmor_error: AppArmor check failed — verify AppArmor installation and tools.
settings.installDesc: Install & Start copies daemon modules under /usr/lib/life-parental/ and /etc/systemd/system/parental-control.service from the app package, runs systemctl enable && start. Requires /usr/bin/node.
settings.warningTestHint: Sets >requestDaemonWarningTest< in >default.json<. The systemd service picks it up on the next tick (~10 s), clears the flag, and opens the same warning window as real alerts.
settings.warningTestQueued: Request saved. If the service is running, the window should appear within a few seconds.
settings.sessionLockHint: After unlocking with a password, the app locks again after inactivity (mouse, keyboard, scroll).
settings.savePrefsSaved: Saved. Applies to the next unlock or immediately if already unlocked.
settings.backupDesc: Export or import a JSON bundle: only top-level keys present in the file are applied; omitted keys leave the system unchanged. For webFilter, blockedApps, and quotas, a missing entries array or a non-array value clears that section (same as []). preferences non-object (e.g. null) removes lockIdleMinutes from config (app default applies). Screen time, web filter, blocked apps, quotas, life modes, session lock, startup flag. Password and usage history are not included.
settings.importConfirmMsg: Import from the selected backup? Only top-level sections present in the file are applied (/etc/hosts + mirror when webFilter is included; schedules, quotas, processWhitelist JSON when present). Omitted sections are left unchanged.
settings.importCompleted: Import completed. Protection state refreshed (open Dashboard to reload family profile buttons).
settings.maintenanceDesc: Screen time and app quotas are enforced by the systemd daemon (no cron). The buttons below only prune old usage JSON or refresh related state. Web filter restore rebuilds the /etc/hosts block from the current settings in default.json. Usage logs removes usage-*, quota-usage-*, and app-usage-* JSON older than 120 days.
settings.quotaScriptRedeployed: Quota script re-deployed; quota exemptions picked up from disk.
settings.webFilterRestored: Web filter restored: /etc/hosts rebuilt from current settings.
settings.regularUserWarning: regular user — system changes will fail; use packaged app with pkexec or npm run dev
settings.customFamilyDesc: Add modes to /etc/life-parental/life-modes.json. Keys must not be school or leisure (those stay built-in). Restart the app or rely on the next Dashboard load to see new buttons.
settings.customFamilyFields: Fields: label (optional), schedule (same shape as Screen Time), mergeCategories / stripCategories (Web Filter category names only), blockedDesktopIds (e.g. firefox.desktop). If mergeCategories is non-empty, stripCategories is ignored for that mode.
settings.dangerZoneDesc: Destructive actions for the whole system profile under /etc/life-parental/.
settings.stopAllDesc: Disables screen time, clears app quotas, unblocks all apps, removes web-filter rules from /etc/hosts (LiFE block), turns off quota exemptions list, and removes KDE kiosk sections from kdeglobals (only if kiosk rules are active — triggers a Plasma session restart then).
settings.stopAllConfirmMsg: Stop and remove ALL LiFE protections? This clears schedules (screen time off), quotas, blocks, web filter hosts block, quota exemptions, and KDE kiosk (if active — session will restart).
settings.allProtectionsRemoved: All protections removed. Refresh sidebar state…
settings.deleteAllUsageDesc: Deletes every usage-*.json, quota-usage-*.json, and app-usage-*.json file in the config directory (all days — screen time and per-app quota logs). Does not change schedules or limits.
settings.deleteHistoryConfirmMsg: Delete ALL screen-time and app-usage daily log files (usage-*.json, quota-usage-*.json, app-usage-*.json)? This cannot be undone.
settings.screenTimeCleanupMsg: Prune old screen-time usage archives under /etc/life-parental/? (Enforcement runs in the LiFE app; there is no cron script to rewrite.)
settings.appQuotaCleanupMsg: Prune old quota usage archives under /etc/life-parental/? (Enforcement runs in the LiFE app.)
settings.quotaExemptionsMsg: Refresh quota-exemption enforcement from current settings and remove legacy life-parental-kill files if present?
settings.pruneLogsMsg: Delete usage-*.json, quota-usage-*.json, and app-usage-*.json in /etc/life-parental/ older than 120 days (by date in the filename)?
settings.webFilterRestoreMsg: Restore web filter: rebuild the /etc/hosts block from the current settings in default.json?

kiosk.title: KDE Kiosk Mode
kiosk.subtitle: Configure lockdown restrictions for KDE Plasma.
kiosk.deactivateConfirmMsg: Remove LiFE kiosk restrictions and restart the KDE session?
kiosk.activateConfirmMsg: Apply and restart the KDE session?

urlRestrictions.desc: Listed folders are blocked for KDE apps using KIO (not a web URL list).
urlRestrictions.eachEntryDesc: Each entry denies open/list for that folder via KDE URL rules (file:).

processWhitelist.title: Quota exemptions
processWhitelist.subtitle: Apps exempt from daily app quota enforcement when time is used up
processWhitelist.enableExemptionsDesc: When on, checked apps are not killed when their daily app quota is exhausted (same minute-based job as App Control). Unchecked apps behave as before. Nothing is blocked from running only because it is missing from this list.
processWhitelist.noAppsWithProcess: No applications with a known process name found.
processWhitelist.exemptionsSaved: Quota exemptions applied; quota script updated.

activityLog.title: Application log
activityLog.desc: Parental action log (newest first). File: /etc/life-parental/activity-log.json (last 400 events kept).
activityLog.screenTimeBonus: Screen time: +{granted} min extra allowance (total +{total} min today)
activityLog.screenTimeBonusLegacy: Screen time bonus (legacy): −{granted} min recorded (now {after} min today)
activityLog.screenTimeReset: Screen time: today's usage file cleared
activityLog.quotaReset: App quotas: today's usage file cleared
activityLog.processWhitelistRedeploy: Quota exemptions: quota script re-deployed from disk
activityLog.kioskApply: KDE kiosk rules written to /etc/xdg/kdeglobals (session restart triggered)
activityLog.kioskStrip: LiFE kiosk sections removed from kdeglobals (session restart triggered)
activityLog.scheduleCronRedeploy: Screen time: enforcement state refreshed from current settings
activityLog.quotaCronRedeploy: App quotas: enforcement state refreshed from current settings
activityLog.embeddedEnforcementRedeploy: Packaged app upgrade: screen-time + quota enforcement redeployed (v{version}{previous})
activityLog.webfilterReapply: Web filter: /etc/hosts block rebuilt from current settings
activityLog.usageArchivesPruned: Old usage archive files removed ({count} files)
activityLog.protectionsStopAll: Danger zone: all protections stopped (screen time, quotas, blocks, web filter, exemptions; kiosk removed if active)
activityLog.usageHistoryWiped: Danger zone: all usage/quota daily logs deleted ({count} files)
